section_summary.extract_value: This conclusion section replicates previous findings that divergent thinking, but not real-world creative achievement, is linked to greater attentional flexibility. It provides novel electrophysiological evidence that this flexibility may involve increased cognitive control processes, as indexed by the N2, even when intelligence is controlled for. In contrast, no association with cognitive control engagement was found for creative achievement, confirming that these two creativity measures rely on different neural mechanisms.
